caseno: Criminal Petition for Leave to Appeal No.27 of 1996.
lawyer:
Md. Joynul Abedin, Advocate instructed by Md. Aftab Hossain, Advocate-on-Record — For the Petitioner. 
Not represented — Respondents.
parties:
Hamidia Oil Mills ----- Petitioner
Vs.
District Anti-Corruption Officer, Chittagong and another ----- Respondents
full_judgment:
Mustafa Kamal J: On 9-9-95 respondent No.1, District Anti-Corruption Officer, Chittagong filed an application before the Sessions Judge, Chittagong being Criminal Miscellaneous Case No.27 of 1995 (Permission) with a prayer for directing the Laldhigi Purbapara Branch of Agrani Bank, where the petitioner has an account, to furnish all connected bank records in connection with an enquiry into an alleged allegation of defalcation of Government money of Taka 30 core. It was disclosed in the application that the petitioner and eight other account-holders of the said Branch of the said bank pledged with the said bank imported goods on obtaining loan, from the said bank, but in collusion with Bank Officials they removed goods worth Taka 30 core without payment of Government dues and defalcated the same. The District Anti-Corruption Bureau, Chittagong has accepted the responsibility of enquiry into the said allegation. In the interest of investigation the Bureau requested the Agrani Bank. Local and Head Office to furnish the connected records of the case, but the Bank Officials are not responding. It was further stated in the application that it was reported that in the audit and departmental enquiry at the Head Office of the Bank the allegation of defalcation of Taka 30 crore had been proved and five Bank Officials had been suspended from service. In the circumstances a prayer was made for seizure of the connected bank records upon permission to be granted by the Court. By Order No.1 dated 11-9-95 the learned Sessions Judge, Chittagong directed the Agrani Bank to deposit to the Bureau of Anti-Corruption, Chittagong all connected records regarding the removal of goods imported upon obtaining loan from the said bank and pleaded with the bank. 

 3. Mr. Md. Joynal Abedin, learned Counsel for the petitioner, submits that the High Court Division failed to consider that in terms of section 94 CrPC a Police Officer or an Anti-Corruption Officer is competent to apply for permission of the Sessions Judge for production of any document from the custody of a bank only when it is necessary for the purpose of investigating an offence under sections 403, 406, 408, 409 and 421 to 424 (both inclusive) and sections 465 to 477A of the Penal Code. He submits that unless there is any pending proceeding by way of lodging any FIR under any of the said sections the Anti-Corruption Officer is not competent to apply for permission from the Sessions Judge. Finally, he submits that the Anti-Corruption Officer did not make out any case for permission for production of the documents from the custody of the bank. 

 4. It is not necessary for the purpose of enquiry into a complaint that a formal case upon lodging an FIR will have to be filed before a Police Officer or an Anti-Corruption Officer can apply for permission to the Sessions Judge for production and seizure of any document. It is necessary for the Sessions Judge, before according permission, to satisfy him that the Police Officer or Anti-Corruption Officer is investigating on an alleged crime and is not merely fishing for information to harass, intimidate or coerce innocent persons. In the present case there is specific information in respect of alleged defalcation of Taka 30 core by several importers in collusion with Bank Officials and also a reference to the fact that the bank's own investigation has revealed that there has been a defalcation.
